title: What Happens If You Knock Out a Tooth?
sources: Cleveland Clinic, 'What To Do When You Knock Out a Tooth' (Todd Coy, DMD, Aug 28 2023) (if the tooth is replaced into the socket or placed in proper storage within five minutes of being knocked out, it's likely it will survive; out of the mouth and dry for more than 60 minutes, its chance for survival decreases significantly; handle the tooth by the crown (the chewing surface), never touch the root; the root contains important fibers called periodontal ligaments, which are necessary for proper healing; don't scrub or soak it; gently push it back into its socket but don't force it; do not put it in water; cover it in milk: the makeup of milk helps maintain the periodontal ligaments; or store it between gums and cheek where saliva moistens it; go immediately to a dentist or the nearest emergency department; baby teeth aren't re-implanted): https://health.clevelandclinic.org/must-act-fast-tooth-gets-knocked/

Mayo Clinic, 'Tooth loss: First aid' (replant an adult tooth right away or as quickly as possible; handle it by the top (crown) only, don't touch the roots; don't scrub it; try to put it back in the socket; if it can't go back in, put it in cow's milk or your own saliva; don't use tap water: too much tap water could kill the cells on the root surface that help reattach the tooth; see a dentist right away, or the emergency department if the office is closed; baby teeth are not replanted): https://www.mayoclinic.org/first-aid/first-aid-tooth-loss/basics/art-20056635

Tease (next video): Mayo Clinic, 'Airplane ear' (a narrow passage called the eustachian tube connects the middle ear to the back of the nose and throat; swallowing or yawning opens it and evens out air pressure): https://www.mayoclinic.org/diseases-conditions/airplane-ear/symptoms-causes/syc-20351701

lines.text: What happens if you knock out a tooth?
Put it back within five minutes, it'll likely survive.
And the backup plan is sitting in your fridge.
lines.caps: AND THE *BACKUP | PLAN IS *SITTING | IN YOUR *FRIDGE
